headline: Revenue grew 10%, 10% and 7% in Q1-Q3 FY2026 as Ratings issuance and ETF fees held up, while disposal gains flatter reported profit and Mobility's spin-off breaks comparability.
summary: S&P Global's first three quarters of FY2026 show revenue growth of 10% in Q1 ($4,171 million) and Q2 ($4,146 million), slowing to 7% in Q3 ($3,678 million) [2]. Q1 and Q2 include Mobility; Q3 is restated without it after the 1 July 2026 spin-off, so dollar levels are not comparable across quarters [2]. Reported profit is inflated by disposal gains of $175 million, $11 million and $200 million [2]. Excluding them (illustrative calculation from 10-Q figures), operating margin was 43.8%, 43.4% and 47.7% [2]. Asset-linked fees rose 18% to $339 million in Q1 [2]. Net cash (debt) moved from $(11,781) million at FY2025 to $(11,024) million at Q3 [3][4]. Consensus FY2026 EPS is $17.94, up 0.4% over 90 days, with 13 estimates raised and 4 cut in 30 days [3]. The earnings releases were not available, so company figures come from the 10-Qs [2]. Consensus data is dated after the 10-K [3][4].
results_commentary:
Q1 FY2026 was the strongest quarter on the thesis KPIs. Revenue rose 10% to $4,171 million from $3,777 million, and asset-linked fees rose 18% to $339 million from $288 million, driven by higher ETF and mutual fund assets under management [2]. Ratings transaction revenue grew on strong investment-grade corporate issuance [2]. Reported operating profit rose 27%, but the 10-Q attributes 14 percentage points of that to a $175 million gain on dispositions; excluding it, operating profit rose 12% and the margin was 43.8% (illustrative calculation: operating profit less the gain, over revenue) against a reported 42% a year earlier [2][3]. Diluted EPS was $4.69 against $3.54, up 32%, and beat consensus by 3.2% [2][3]. Q2 FY2026 held the growth rate but missed on earnings. Revenue rose 10% to $4,146 million from $3,755 million, with the same Ratings and Indices drivers [2]. Diluted EPS was $4.12 against $3.50, up 18%, but it missed the consensus estimate by 2.9% [2][3]. The miss followed $79 million of disposition-related costs and $44 million of employee severance in the quarter, which the 10-Q lists as operating items [2]. Excluding the $11 million gain, the margin was 43.4% (illustrative calculation) against a reported 41% a year earlier [2].

Q3 FY2026 is where growth slowed. Revenue rose 7% to $3,678 million from $3,443 million on the restated, continuing-operations basis [2]. The 10-Q names two sources of support: Ratings corporate bond issuance and Indices asset-linked fees, and retroactive revenue from delayed renewals at Market Intelligence [2]. The filing does not quantify the retroactive amount, so the underlying growth rate cannot be separated from it. Within Ratings, bank loan revenue and structured finance revenue both declined [2]. Excluding the $200 million gain, the margin was about 47.7% (illustrative calculation) against a reported 45% a year earlier, and ex-gain operating profit rose 8% [2]. The margin gain partly reflects the removal of Mobility from the Q3 base, which the filing does not quantify. Diluted EPS from continuing operations was $4.45 against $3.54, up 26% [2]. Footnote on EPS figures: the Q3 FY2026 10-Q gives $3.54 as the Q3 FY2025 comparative, which this update uses. The scorecard shows $3.86 for the same quarter a year earlier [3]. The filing does not explain the gap, and this update gives no reason for it. Two other Q3 FY2026 EPS figures also conflict: $4.25 in the scorecard and $4.58 in the consensus surprise data [3]. This update uses the 10-Q figure of $4.45.

Deterioration appeared in the balance-sheet measures against the year-ago quarter. The current ratio was 0.74x at Q3 against 0.97x a year earlier, and net debt was $(11,024) million against $(10,194) million [3]. Against the FY2025 year-end, funding improved: cash and short-term investments rose to $2,441 million from $1,801 million, and total debt fell to $13,465 million from $13,582 million [3][4]. Share count fell 4.4% year on year to 289.9 million [3].

thesis_check.thesis: T1: Indices asset-linked fees keep growing at mid-teens rates as ETF assets compound, so Indices remains the main earnings driver.
thesis_check.signpost: Indices asset-linked fee growth of at least 10% reported in the FY2026 10-K (about February 2027). Interim test: ETF AUM rising, not falling, each quarter.
thesis_check.evidence: Q1 FY2026 asset-linked fees rose 18% to $339 million from $288 million, and the 10-Q links this to higher ETF and mutual fund AUM [2]. Q2 and Q3 MD&A cite higher ETF AUM and higher asset-linked fees, but the excerpts give no quarterly fee figures, so these quarters are rated on narrative only [2]. Final test is the FY2026 10-K [4].

thesis_check.thesis: T2: Shareholder payouts above free cash flow are not sustainable without disposal proceeds, so leverage keeps rising.
thesis_check.signpost: FY2026 buybacks plus dividends at or below free cash flow, and total debt growth below 10%, in the FY2026 10-K (about February 2027).
thesis_check.evidence: Q1 net cash widened to $(11,966) million from $(11,781) million at FY2025, consistent with the thesis [3][4]. By Q3, total debt was $13,465 million against $13,582 million at FY2025, and net debt narrowed to $(11,024) million, helped by $386 million of nine-month disposal gains and a cash build to $2,441 million [2][3]. Leverage has not risen in FY2026 so far, so the Q3 status is intact, not weakened. The payout-versus-FCF signpost cannot be tested until the FY2026 10-K, because the 10-Qs do not show quarterly buyback or dividend totals [2]. The invalidation test (debt above $15 billion) is not met.

thesis_check.thesis: T3: The current valuation requires revenue growth to return to historical rates, which consensus does not yet forecast.
thesis_check.signpost: FY2026 consensus EPS at or above $17.94 with more analysts raising than cutting estimates over the next 30 days, confirmed at the FY2026 results (about February 2027).
thesis_check.evidence: Revenue growth was 10%, 10% and 7% in Q1, Q2 and Q3, all below the 11.9% growth implied by the reverse DCF and the 11.1% three-year CAGR, so growth has not returned to historical rates [2][3][4]. Current FY2026 consensus EPS is $17.94, unchanged from the signpost level, with 13 raises and 4 cuts in the last 30 days, and FY2027 consensus is $20.15, 0.4% lower over 90 days with 11 raises and 11 cuts [3]. The FY2026 signpost is met at the current consensus level but is not yet confirmed. Consensus data is dated after the 10-K.

thesis_check.thesis: T4: Regulatory and legal costs will not erode the 42% operating margin, so the margin story holds despite supervision in Ratings, Indices and Energy.
thesis_check.signpost: Operating margin excluding disposal gains of at least 40% in the FY2026 10-K (about February 2027).
thesis_check.evidence: Reported operating margin was 48% in Q1, 44% in Q2 and 53% in Q3 [2]. Excluding disposal gains, the margin is 43.8%, 43.4% and 47.7% (illustrative calculation from 10-Q operating profit less gains, over revenue), all above the 40% signpost [2]. The Q3 step-up is partly a mix effect of removing Mobility, which the filing does not quantify [2]. The 10-Qs disclose no new regulatory fine or legal charge; legal costs in the year-ago quarters were $29 million in Q2 2025 and $13 million in Q3 2025 [2].

risk_update: Materialised: the Mobility spin-off completed on 1 July 2026 and reduced reported revenue from Q3, so reported figures are no longer like-for-like [2]. Disposal activity was heavy: the Enterprise Data Management and thinkFolio sales in January 2026 reduced Market Intelligence revenue, and disposition-related costs were $118 million in the first half and $12 million in the first nine months [2]. Severance of $44 million was booked in Q2 [2]. Ratings structured finance and bank loan revenue declined in Q3, which is the transaction-linked exposure named in the annual risk section [2][4]. Eased: funding pressure narrowed, with cash up to $2,441 million and total debt down to $13,465 million at Q3 [3]. Unchanged: the 10-Qs refer back to the 10-K for risk factors and disclose no new cyber, regulatory or fine exposure, so the annual-report risks are carried forward without update [2][4]. The current ratio of 0.74x at Q3 stays below 1 [3]. The releases were not available, so no guidance changes can be confirmed.
outlook: The provided releases contain no guidance: the 8-K exhibits were not available, and the 10-Q MD&A excerpts do not state guidance, so none is reported here. Consensus FY2026 revenue is $14,716.7 million, down 4.0% from FY2025's $15,336.0 million; the filings do not say how consensus treats Mobility, and the nine-month recast growth is +9% [3][2]. FY2026 EPS consensus is $17.94 (range $17.68 to $18.78), up 0.4% over 90 days, and FY2027 is $20.15, down 0.4% [3]. At $455.17 the forward P/E is 25.4x [3]. Watch: Q4 FY2026 growth without the retroactive renewal benefit, the ETF-linked asset-fee figure for Q2 and Q3 (not in the excerpts), whether buybacks stay at or below free cash flow, and the FY2026 10-K in February 2027, which tests all four signposts.
